explanation: An ancient people and empire in Mesopotamia, known for their military power and conquests.
A city on the coast of the Mediterranean Sea, now part of Israel, which was attacked and besieged by the Assyrians.
A high-ranking military officer in the Assyrian Empire who led the attack on Ashdod.
King of Assyria (722–705 BC), who sent Tartan to conquer Ashdod.
The prophet to whom the book's message is attributed, and who delivered God's warnings and promises to the people of Israel.
Symbolizes vulnerability and humiliation, and in this case shows how God intends to punish Egypt and Cush for their pride and reliance on their own power.
An ancient empire in Northeast Africa that was often in conflict with Israel and other nations in the region.
A region south of Egypt, in present-day Sudan, which had close political and cultural ties with Egypt.
